newsitem.title: USA: Wheat harvest going strong in southern Kansas.
newsitem.headline: Wheat harvest going strong in southern Kansas.

text.p: Wheat harvest was in full swing in southern Kansas during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
Five percent of the state's wheat was harvested, against 18 percent last year and 16 percent on average.

Wheat condition improved and was rated 14 percent excellent, 54 good, 23 fair, six poor and three very poor. That compared to the previous week's rating of eight percent excellent, 52 good, 28 fair, nine poor and three percent very poor.
Thirty-six percent of the wheat was ripe, behind 42 percent last year and the five-year average of 46 percent.
Sorghum was 90 percent planted, against 92 percent last year and the average of 82 percent. Soybeans were 98 percent seeded, ahead of 88 last year the average of 81 percent.
Corn condition also improved and was rated 23 percent excellent, 63 good, 13 fair, one poor and nil very poor.
Seventy-five percent of the state's sunflower crop was planted. Condition of the crop was 10 percent excellent, 79 good and 11 percent fair.
Pasture condition improved and was rated 13 percent excellent, 67 good, 17 fair and three percent poor.
